misclassified_entities.recommendation: Reclassify as internal process or remove external designation

misclassified_entities.recommendation: Reclassify as internal state or remove external designation

misclassified_entities.recommendation: Reclassify as internal component or remove external designation

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Ethereum Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peer establishing eth/70 protocol connection. No cryptographic attestation of advertised capabilities. Peers can lie about block availability, send malformed data, or attempt Sybil attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Requesting Block Range
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Connected peer querying for block availability information. Request parameters are untrusted and can be used for reconnaissance or DoS attempts.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer whose block range claims have not been verified. Can advertise false block ranges to waste bandwidth, disrupt sync, or mislead peer selection algorithms.

trusted_external_entities.name: Coordinated Malicious Peers
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Multiple attacker-controlled nodes advertising false block ranges. Sybil attack vector that could partition the network or prevent honest block range discovery.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User or application submitting an access list transaction. Can provide arbitrary transaction data, malformed access lists, or attempt gas exploitation attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer node or client that submitted the transaction. Transaction bytes are untrusted and must be fully validated before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External client querying for logs via eth_getLogs or similar RPC. Query parameters are untrusted and can be used for DoS or resource exhaustion attacks.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: TCP connection establishment does not imply trust. Protocol handshake must validate peer identity and capabilities before full communication.
Incoming block range requests must be rate-limited and validated. Responding reveals local block availability which could aid targeted attacks.
Block range claims are unverified assertions. Must be validated through actual block requests. Track peer reliability over time.
ATTACK VECTOR: Coordinated false range advertisements can disrupt sync. Mitigation requires diverse peer selection and range verification.
Transaction bytes are untrusted. Full validation of transaction type, format, signature, and access list structure required before processing.
Raw transaction bytes from network are completely untrusted. Must validate transaction type, RLP encoding, field counts, and all structural requirements.
Log query parameters are untrusted. Bloom filter provides pre-filtering but false positives require full log verification. Query complexity must be bounded.
